newsitem.title: USA: Clinton hails EU move to promote Cuban democracy.
newsitem.headline: Clinton hails EU move to promote Cuban democracy.

text.p: President Clinton on Monday hailed the European Union's moves to promote democracy in Cuba.
"I applaud the European Union for the important step foward it has taken by adopting a common position on Cuba," Clinton told a joint news conference with EU leaders.
The EU pledged Saturday to push for democracy in Cuba, threatening to suspend any future trade agreement with Havana if it saw a serious breach of human rights.
The new EU stance has been brought on in part as a reaction to the United States' Helms-Burton law, an amalgam of anti-Cuban legislation.
Washington wants its partners to take stronger action against Havana but has infuriated most of them by threatening actions against foreign firms that do certain kinds of business on the island.
Clinton has suspended until February 1 the right for U.S. companies and individuals to file suits against foreigners who do business with assets in Cuba expropriated from Americans.

Asked if Monday's meeting with EU leaders meant that Washington would not implement Helms-Burton and the EU would drop its efforts to oppose the law at the World Trade Organization, Clinton replied, "I don't think it necessarily means either one."
He said he had not received a final recommendation on whether or not to go ahead with implementation of Helms Burton and that no decision had been made.

European Commission President Jacques Santer said the two sides share the same target with regards to Cuba but differ on the means. He added that the EU was sticking with its decision to pursue the issue at the WTO.
